content.title: About
content.content: Buckwheat flour is made from whole buckwheat grains that are finely milled. It has a distinct nutty aroma, light brown color, and a slightly dense texture. It is used in baking, pancakes, breading, and as a thickener for sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Buckwheat is not a true cereal but belongs to the buckwheat family, making it a pseudocereal.
Buckwheat flour is rich in rutin, an antioxidant that supports blood vessel health.
In Russia, buckwheat is traditionally considered a “winter” food, and its flour is popular in colder regions.
Buckwheat flour is naturally gluten‑free, suitable for gluten‑free diets.
In Japan, buckwheat flour is used to make the classic noodle “soba.”

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Buckwheat flour provides about 13 % protein, including all essential amino acids.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps stabilize blood sugar levels, beneficial for people with diabetes.

items.title: Mineral dense
items.content: Contains magnesium, iron, phosphorus, and zinc, important for bones and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Rutin and quercetin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to buckwheat.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking or sprouting grains before milling is recommended.

items.title: Digestive reactions
items.content: Large portions may cause gas or bloating in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Buckwheat flour is used in pancakes, crepes, breads, muffins, and as a coating for fish or meat. It can be blended with other gluten‑free flours for a lighter texture. Substitute it 1:1 for wheat flour to boost nutritional value.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
